radiology_report:
Maastricht UMC+ | Radiology | 05 Jan 2025 | mpMRI Prostate
Clinical indication: 68-year-old male with rising PSA (12.0 ng/mL) and prior negative TRUS biopsy. Re-evaluation requested.
FINDINGS:
The gland spans 52.0 mL in total volume. T2 sequences isolate a sharply hypointense focus, reaching 18 mm at its widest point, situated in the right mid-gland peripheral zone. Diffusion restriction accompanies markedly reduced ADC signals. DCE imaging captures an early, localized enhancement pattern against the surrounding tissue. Seminal vesicles retain normal appearance. Capsular integrity remains intact, with no suspicious nodal enlargement. The bladder and distal rectum show no abnormalities.
IMPRESSION:
Focal lesion in the right mid-gland peripheral zone consistent with PI-RADS 4.
Prostate volume 52.0 mL; PSA density 0.23 ng/mL/mL.
csPCa predicted probability 0.51779693.

previous_notes.author: Dr. H. Martens (GP)
previous_notes.text: Clinical update for ongoing urological follow-up subsequent to last year’s negative biopsy. PSA climbed to 12.3 ng/mL during June, accompanied by a free-to-total ratio of 10%. Due to sustained elevation and moderate lower urinary tract symptoms managed with tamsulosin, a referral to the urology outpatient clinic was processed. Systemic health remains stable, with cholesterol well-regulated and renal parameters unchanged.
